title: LLM Logbook Schema
description: Schema for tracking development context across sessions. Supports long-term memory, objective tracking with actionable guidance, and progress documentation. Designed for continuity across multiple LLMs and sessions.
$comment: CANONICAL SHAPE (read this if you forked or adopted Waves mid-flight — the contract lives here, not only in $defs). objectives is an object with exactly two arrays: objectives.main and objectives.secondary. objectives.main is an ARRAY of OBJECTS, each with an integer `id` (start at 1, increment) plus content/context/scope/status — NOT a single object, NOT a string. There is NO 'meta', NO 'context' at the root, NO 'completed_at', NO 'ui_requirements', NO 'philosophy' field. completion_guide exists ONLY on secondary objectives, never on main. An undeclared sibling field is the signal you are writing in the wrong artifact: durable strategy → roadmap; the product WHY → blueprint; rolling memory → recent_context/history_summary here. If a value won't fit a declared field, the field is wrong, not the cap.

ticket.description: Metadata of the ticket or task that anchors this logbook. This is the ultimate goal that all objectives contribute to.
ticket.$comment: Populate from user input or external system. If no ticket URL exists, leave url empty. Title and description are required to create the logbook.

title.description: Title of the ticket or task. Should be concise and descriptive.
title.$comment: Copy from ticket system or ask user. Keep under 100 characters.

url.description: Direct URL to the ticket or task in an external system (Jira, GitHub, etc.).
url.$comment: Optional. Leave empty string if no external system. Do not invent URLs.

external_ref.description: Structured reference to the ticket in an external tracker, when a plain url is insufficient (e.g. an Azure DevOps work-item id, a Linear issue).
external_ref.$comment: Optional. Officializes the ado_wi_id / external-id field adopters invented. STOP: one external system per logbook; if the work spans two trackers, that is two logbooks. REDIRECT: the human link goes in `url`; the ticket prose in `description`; do NOT add system-specific custom keys here. `system` is a free string (no closed enum — validating a specific tracker is the command's job, not the schema's). bad: {'azure_id': 867, 'jira': 'X'} (two systems + custom keys). good: {'system': 'azure-devops', 'id': '867', 'url': 'https://...'}.

system.description: Name of the external tracker (free string), e.g. 'azure-devops', 'github', 'jira', 'linear'.

id.description: Identifier of the work item within that system.

url.description: Direct link to the work item (may duplicate ticket.url).

ui_requirements.description: UI scope of the ticket, when it involves frontend work. Optional. Officializes the field logbook-create Step 2.1 already emits (corpus: present in 22/22 logbooks, previously undeclared).
ui_requirements.$comment: Optional. STOP: describe UI SCOPE only — whether there is UI, the references, brief notes. REDIRECT: implementation steps go in the secondaries' completion_guide; visual design decisions -> a product_decision or the design doc; do NOT paste full specs here. bad: a paragraph of layout CSS. good: {has_ui: true, visual_references: ['designs/detail.png'], notes: '3-column grid on desktop'}.

has_ui.description: True if the ticket involves UI work.

visual_references.description: Paths or URLs to mocks, wireframes, screenshots.

notes.description: Brief UI analysis or layout notes.

description.description: Detailed explanation and context provided in the ticket. Includes acceptance criteria if available.
description.$comment: DISTILL, don't dump. Goal + acceptance in 2-4 sentences: what 'done' looks like from the user's view, the anchor (NOT the design). REDIRECT: the implementation spec (that is objectives + completion_guide), file/class inventories (scope.files), and references to past decisions/why-this-approach (governance_context.relevant_decisions). The full design belongs DOWNWARD in objectives — this field just frames the target. Test: if it reads like a how-to or grows by hundreds of chars per wave, you pasted the spec; cut to the goal + acceptance. bad: 'Refactor auth: create UserDto, migrate table 011, add UserRepository.findByEmail returning Result<User>, wire AuthDataSource, then add JWT middleware reading the header, plus tests for...' (1900 chars). good: 'Add email/password sign-up so a new user can authenticate. Done when a valid sign-up creates a user and returns a session token, and a duplicate email is rejected with a clear error.'

objectives.description: Project objectives organized by priority. Main objectives define high-level deliverables with scope. Secondary objectives are actionable steps with specific completion guidance.
objectives.$comment: Both main and secondary arrays can be populated in the same operation. Secondary objectives should have completion_guide based on code analysis using main objectives' scope.files as reference points.

main.description: Primary objectives that define major deliverables. Each provides context, reference files, and applicable rules.
main.$comment: Use project_manifest.json to identify related layers and features. Each main objective needs: verifiable content, business context, scope with reference files, and applicable rules from project_rules.json.

secondary.description: Actionable objectives derived from analysis of main objectives. Each contains specific guidance for implementation.
secondary.$comment: Base completion_guide on code inspection starting from main objectives' scope.files. Apply scope.rules when writing guidance. All secondary objectives contribute to ticket completion.

recent_context.description: Running log of recent interactions, findings, decisions, and progress. Newest entries at index 0. Sliding window that compacts to history_summary when full.
recent_context.$comment: Prepend new entries at index 0. When array exceeds maxItems, remove last (oldest) entry and summarize it to history_summary. Never replace entire array.

items.description: Single context entry representing a meaningful interaction, finding, or decision.
items.$comment: Create entry for: progress updates, important findings, decisions made, blockers encountered, user instructions. Keep content focused and actionable.

id.description: Unique identifier for this entry. Immutable once created.
id.$comment: Start at 1, increment by 1 globally across all entries. Never reuse IDs.

created_at.description: UTC timestamp when entry was created (ISO 8601). Immutable.
created_at.$comment: Set once at creation. Never modify.

content.description: Entry content describing action, decision, finding, or progress. Should be meaningful and provide context for future sessions.
content.$comment: Write concisely but completely. Include: what happened, why it matters, any decisions made. Future agents will use this to understand context.

mood.description: User's emotional state during this entry if observable (focused, frustrated, excited, uncertain).
mood.$comment: Optional. Only populate if user mood is clearly observable. Helps future agents adjust communication style.

history_summary.description: Compact summaries of entries removed from recent_context. Preserves continuity when short-term memory is full. Newest at index 0.
history_summary.$comment: Write here ONLY when truncating recent_context. Summarize removed entry in max 140 chars. Prepend at index 0. If exceeds maxItems, remove oldest (last) entry.

items.description: Compressed summary of a removed recent_context entry.
items.$comment: Capture essential information only: what was done, key decision, or important finding.

id.description: Unique identifier for this summary. Immutable once created.
id.$comment: Start at 1, increment by 1. Separate sequence from recent_context IDs.

created_at.description: UTC timestamp when summary was created (ISO 8601). Immutable.
created_at.$comment: Set once at creation. Never modify.

content.description: Compressed summary of removed entry. Must capture essential information.
content.$comment: Summarize in tweet-length. Focus on: what was done, outcome, or key decision. Omit details recoverable from code.

mood.description: User's emotional state at time of original entry if it was recorded.
mood.$comment: Optional. Preserve from original entry if present.

future_reminders.description: User-created reminders for future sessions. Agent surfaces these when their time arrives.
future_reminders.$comment: Only add reminders when user explicitly requests. Check this array at session start and surface any due reminders.

items.description: A scheduled reminder to surface in a future session.
items.$comment: Create only on explicit user request. Remove after surfacing to user.

id.description: Unique identifier for this reminder. Immutable once created.
id.$comment: Start at 1, increment by 1. Never reuse IDs.

created_at.description: UTC timestamp when reminder was created (ISO 8601). Immutable.
created_at.$comment: Set once at creation. Never modify.

content.description: Reminder message to surface to user when due.
content.$comment: Write exactly what user wants to be reminded about. Include any context needed.

when.description: UTC timestamp when this reminder should be surfaced to user.
when.$comment: Compare against current time at session start. Surface if current time >= when.

governance_context.description: Compact extracted subset of the blueprint chain (scope → product → company) that impacts this logbook's business direction. Populated by logbook-create A1.4 via deterministic jq queries against each blueprint in the parent_blueprint chain. Loaded into objectives-implement Step 5 'Governance banner' so implementers carry blueprint-level alignment without re-reading full blueprints.
governance_context.$comment: Replaces the previous vague 'extract relevant sections' directive. Each item carries a `level` field (scope|product|company) indicating which blueprint in the chain it came from. The banner printed at implementation time uses this field verbatim — same pattern as project_rules.json injection into completion_guide. Forward-only: pre-existing logbooks without this field continue to validate; new logbooks populate it. Empty arrays are valid when no blueprint matches the ticket (rare but possible for greenfield tickets).

blueprint_chain.description: Ordered list of blueprints walked by logbook-create starting from the scope/product blueprint and following parent_blueprint refs upward. company_blueprint.json appended last when present.

path.description: Path relative to repo root, e.g. 'projects/frontend/waves_files/blueprint.json'.

matched_capabilities.description: Capabilities (essential + non_essential.important + non_essential.desired) whose `capability` text matches ticket keywords or whose ID is referenced by matched flows. Includes is_essential flag + acceptance_criteria when present.

related_flows.description: user_flows + system_flows touching matched_capabilities (via capability_refs intersection). Abbreviated form: name + entry_point + termination + description (no exhaustive step lists).

governing_design_principles.description: design_principles that generated rules referenced in logbook's primaries' scope.rules. Surfaces the WHY behind coding rules — implementer reads principle + rule together.

applicable_product_rules.description: product_rules whose applies_to references matched_capabilities or matched flows. Distinct from coding rules (project_rules.json) — these are business behavioral rules.

out_of_scope_reminders.description: out_of_scope items whose statement text overlaps with ticket keywords. Surfaced as STOP signals — if implementer is about to do this, abort.

relevant_decisions.description: product_decisions whose impact_on references matched capabilities/flows, OR whose decision text directly forbids/requires something in the ticket territory. Surfaces historical 'do/don't' to prevent re-litigation.

success_metrics.description: success_metrics tied to matched_capabilities (when blueprint declares the linkage). Informs instrumentation + observability choices.

autonomous_entity_identity.description: Populated only when any blueprint in the chain has blueprint_type='autonomous_entity'. Carries identity + voice + operation_modes + operational_limits — load-bearing for agentic ticket implementations.

audit.description: Audit state for this logbook. Models the three gates as first-class objects: integrity (logbook-create Step A6), correctness_postplan (Step A7), correctness_postimpl (objectives-implement Step 9.8). Legacy fields is_already_audited/audit_file are the v2 shape, preserved for backwards-compat.
audit.$comment: CANONICAL SHAPE (v3): three optional sub-objects — integrity, correctness_postplan, correctness_postimpl — each a gate_result {ran, report_file, summary, completed_at}. STOP: one gate per sub-object; do not merge a post-plan finding into integrity. REDIRECT: the findings prose lives in the report_file on disk (corpus-mineable, design_principle #11), NOT inline here; a numeric tally goes in summary; the logbook's running narrative goes in recent_context. Legacy {is_already_audited, audit_file} stay valid (v2) until migrate_v2_to_v3 (w6 Phase 4) maps them to integrity.{ran, report_file}. bad: stuffing the A7 finding list into a $-field on the logbook. good: correctness_postplan = {ran:true, report_file:'.../audits/correctness-postplan-<basename>.json', summary:{critical:0,warning:2}, completed_at:'...'}.

is_already_audited.description: Legacy (v2). True once the integrity reviewer has run at least once and findings were processed. Set back to false in logbook-update on material changes. v3 reads integrity.ran; this flag is kept for backwards-compat.

audit_file.description: Legacy (v2). Relative path to the most recent integrity audit report JSON. Superseded by integrity.report_file in v3; kept for backwards-compat.
audit_file.$comment: The reviewer overwrites the same audit file path on re-audit; copy it first if history is needed. migrate_v2_to_v3 maps this to integrity.report_file.

recommendations.description: Recommendations discovered during implementation. These are improvements or follow-ups that aren't blocking but should be considered.
recommendations.$comment: Populated by objectives-implement command when code-implementer finds opportunities for improvement. Review periodically.

created_at.description: UTC timestamp when recommendation was created.

from_objective.description: ID of the objective that generated this recommendation (e.g., '1.1').

affected_files.description: Files that would be affected by implementing this recommendation.

priority.description: Priority level for addressing this recommendation.

main_objective.description: High-level objective defining a major deliverable. Provides business context, reference files as starting points for code tracing, and applicable project rules.
main_objective.$comment: Use project_manifest.json to identify related layers and features. Populate scope.files with entry points for code analysis. Populate scope.rules with applicable rule IDs from project_rules.json (empty array if no rules exist).

id.description: Unique identifier for this main objective. Immutable once created.
id.$comment: Start at 1, increment by 1. Never reuse IDs even after abandonment.

created_at.description: UTC timestamp when objective was created (ISO 8601). Immutable.
created_at.$comment: Set once at creation. Never modify.

content.description: Verifiable outcome statement that serves as acceptance criteria. When this statement is true, the objective is achieved.
content.$comment: ONE verifiable outcome per objective. Write as outcome, not task; answer 'Is this done?' yes/no by inspecting code. STOP: split it when multi-concern: a '+' or ' y '/' and ', an em-dash carrying a design choice ('— Modelo A: ...'), a colon-list, a file/class inventory, or two verbs. >180 chars is almost always more than one concern. REDIRECT: the design choice → context; the proof/tests → verification_demonstrations (and secondary.test_cases); a second deliverable → a SECOND main objective. bad: 'Refactor pricing engine — Modelo A: tabla CTE; tests exhaustivos de bordes' (task + design + tests = 3 concerns). good: 'Pricing engine computes tiered totals correctly' (design → context, tests → verification_demonstrations).

context.description: Business or technical rationale: who needs this, what problem it solves, relevant constraints or dependencies.
context.$comment: The business/technical WHY only — who needs it, what constraint forces the approach. REDIRECT: implementation steps/how (→ completion_guide), file lists (→ scope.files), rule IDs already stored in scope.rules (do NOT re-list them), and planning-process scratch labels ('Dimensión N', 'Mindset:', 'orthogonality_review' — those leak from the planning prompt and are not durable context). Test: delete every proper-noun class name; if no 'why' remains, you wrote 'how' in the wrong field. bad: 'Dimensión 2. Mindset: defensivo. Usar CTE recursivo con jitter = base*2^n, aplica rules #4 #7, tocar pricing_repo.dart...' (planning meta + how + rule re-list). good: 'Sales needs tiered pricing because enterprise contracts negotiate volume bands; current flat rate blocks the deal.'

scope.description: Implementation boundaries: starting point files for code tracing and project rules that constrain the solution.
scope.$comment: Files are entry points for deeper analysis, not exhaustive lists. Rules guide implementation approach.

files.description: Reference files identified during initial analysis. Entry points for deeper code tracing.
files.$comment: Use relative paths from project root. Append '(new)' for files to create. Example: 'src/dtos/ProductDTO.ts (new)'.

rules.description: IDs from project_rules.json that apply to this objective's scope. Empty array if project has no rules defined.
rules.$comment: Reference rules by ID. Apply these rules when implementing. If no rules exist, use the most common best practices for the framework and language always applying YAGNI principle.

status.description: Current state: not_started (pending work), active (in progress), blocked (waiting on external input), achieved (completed), abandoned (cancelled).
status.$comment: Set only ONE main objective as 'active' at a time. Use 'blocked' when waiting for user input or external dependency. Set 'achieved' ONLY when content statement is verified true AND all entries in verification_demonstrations have verdict='pass' (design_principle #8 — see field $comment for protocol).

verification_demonstrations.description: Observable executable evidence that this primary outcome was achieved. Required on every NEW primary (forward-only per blueprint decision #15). Status='achieved' requires verdict='pass' on every entry. Empty/absent only on grandfathered historical logbooks.
verification_demonstrations.$comment: design_principle #8 (Demonstration over declaration). PROTOCOL (logbook-create Phase 4 w4): A4.5 verification-designer (fresh subagent, blocking) proposes type-aware demonstrations per primary based on scope.files extensions + content keywords (e.g., .dart/.ts→unit_test; .json schemas→schema_validation; .md skills→sandbox_execution+behavior_check; release/tag→release_verification). A4.6 feasibility-checker (fresh subagent, blocking) verifies local deps with deterministic checks (command -v, gh auth status); if missing_deps detected, A4 inserts provisioning secondaries BEFORE implementation — blocks 'paper demonstrations' by construction. Both subagents are UNCONDITIONAL (no primary skips A4.5+A4.6; if a primary cannot be expressed as verifiable it is ill-defined and must be re-formulated). Schema-level the field is optional to preserve forward-only (historical logbooks grandfathered); mandatory at gate-time. Bootstrap: Phase 1 w4 logbook (which builds this field) applies the principle in prose via completion_guide. DRY with test_cases (product_rule #10): when a primary's secondaries declared test_cases, the demonstration REFERENCES the suite covering them ('suite covering these cases passes, verdict=pass') and does NOT re-enumerate — test_cases SPECIFY (design), verification_demonstrations PROVE (achievement). Enumerate once, prove once.

items.description: Single verification demonstration: one observable, executable check tied to an acceptance criterion of the primary.
items.$comment: Each entry binds a verification TYPE to a concrete TARGET and an EXPECTED observable outcome. command_or_method must be deterministic for non-adversarial types. verdict='pending' until executed; flip to 'pass' or 'fail' with evidence.

type.description: Verification taxonomy (10 types). Software-leaning: unit_test, integration_test. Agentic/cross-format: sandbox_execution, schema_validation, behavior_check. Cross-cutting: release_verification (tag/release published), state_change_verification (file/config/db delta), external_observation (3rd party API/visible artifact), documentation_consistency (docs vs reality), adversarial_review (fresh-subagent critique with value lens).
type.$comment: A4.5 verification-designer infers type from primary's scope.files + content keywords. Pattern matching examples: .dart/.ts/.py → unit_test or integration_test; .json schemas → schema_validation + sandbox_execution (jq/ajv); .md commands/skills → sandbox_execution + behavior_check; .sh hooks → sandbox_execution; tag/release keywords → release_verification (gh api); settings/config changes → state_change_verification (jq query before/after).

target.description: Concrete artifact being verified — file path, function name, schema name, command, tag identifier, URL.
target.$comment: Reference the actual artifact, not a description. Examples: 'plugin/skills/waves-protocol/references/logbook_software_schema.json', 'WavesStubCheck.detectEmptyBody', 'v3.0.0 git tag', 'POST /api/products endpoint'.

expected.description: Observable outcome that proves the demonstration passes. Must be checkable and bound to an acceptance criterion of the primary.
expected.$comment: Concrete, not aspirational. Examples: 'jq empty exits 0', 'ajv validate returns valid=true', 'gh api repos/owner/repo/releases/tags/v3.0.0 returns HTTP 200', 'critic verdict in [confirmed, gold]'. Avoid 'should work', 'looks correct', 'no errors'.

command_or_method.description: Deterministic command, script invocation, or subagent prompt that executes this demonstration. May be empty only when type='adversarial_review' (method described inline in evidence).
command_or_method.$comment: Shell command for deterministic types; brief subagent role description for adversarial_review. Examples: 'jq empty plugin/skills/.../schema.json', 'ajv validate -s schema.json -d fixture.json', 'gh api repos/exovian-developments/waves-cowork-plugin/tags', 'critic subagent reviewing test for circular assertions'.

verdict.description: Execution outcome of this demonstration. status='achieved' on the primary REQUIRES verdict='pass' on ALL entries.
verdict.$comment: Stays 'pending' until objectives-implement Step 7.5 critic runs the demonstration. Flip to 'pass' when expected matches observed; 'fail' otherwise with reason in evidence. NEVER leave 'pending' when marking primary as achieved — the gate blocks.

verified_at.description: UTC ISO 8601 timestamp when verdict was recorded. Absent while verdict='pending'.
verified_at.$comment: Set ONCE when verdict flips from 'pending'. Immutable after. Used by audits to detect stale verdicts vs current artifact state.

evidence.description: Observable proof supporting the verdict: command stdout snippet, file diff summary, URL of public artifact, subagent classification with rationale.
evidence.$comment: Concrete and auditable. Examples for pass: 'jq exit 0 on file (256 lines)', 'ajv: valid=true', 'critic verdict=confirmed — substance matches acceptance criterion'. For fail: error line + reason. Required when verdict != 'pending'.

gate_result.description: Result of one audit/review gate (integrity, correctness post-plan, correctness post-impl), persisted as a first-class object so the corpus miner can read it across logbooks.
gate_result.$comment: STOP: one gate run per object — do not accumulate multiple runs here (the report_file is overwritten; copy it first if history is needed). REDIRECT: the full findings list lives in the file at report_file (design_principle #11 — analyses are persisted, not ephemeral); summary holds only compact counts/verdict; the logbook's narrative goes in recent_context. bad: 'summary': {note: 'several issues, see chat'} (prose, ephemeral). good: 'ran': true, 'report_file': 'waves_files/waves/wN/audits/correctness-postplan-phase_1.json', 'summary': {critical: 0, warning: 6}, 'completed_at': '2026-05-30T00:00:00Z'.

ran.description: True if this gate executed for the current logbook state (it may still have executed INCOMPLETE — see degraded).

report_file.description: Relative path to the persisted analysis JSON for this gate, e.g. 'waves_files/waves/wN/audits/<gate>-<basename>.json'.

summary.description: Compact counts/verdict for quick reading (e.g. {critical, warning} or {confirmed, smoke}). Full detail lives in report_file.

completed_at.description: UTC timestamp when this gate completed.

degraded.description: True when the gate executed INCOMPLETE: one or more reviewer lenses (or their verifier B) fell — failed, timed out, returned non-JSON, or reported unreadable_input. ran:true + degraded:true means 'executed but its coverage claim is partial'. A degraded gate blocks the logbook's completion claim (no resolution-create) until the fallen lens re-runs or a correctness_gate_override is documented in resolved_decisions.

fallen_reviewers.description: Names of the lenses that fell when degraded:true (e.g. 'waves-coverage-gap-analyzer'). Empty/absent when the gate ran complete.

secondary_objective.description: Actionable objective derived from code analysis. Contains specific implementation guidance based on actual code inspection.
secondary_objective.$comment: Base completion_guide on code inspection using main objectives' scope.files as starting points. Reference specific files, patterns, and applicable rules in the guide.

id.description: Unique identifier across all secondary objectives. Immutable once created.
id.$comment: Start at 1, increment globally across all secondary objectives. Never reuse IDs.

parent_main_id.description: Id of the main objective this secondary serves. Secondaries are a flat list; this links each one to its primary.
parent_main_id.$comment: Optional (backwards-compat: pre-existing logbooks have a flat list with no link). STOP: one parent per secondary — a secondary that serves two primaries is two secondaries. REDIRECT: this is the structural primary->secondary link only; rule inheritance still flows from the parent's scope.rules, not from here. bad: parent_main_id pointing at a non-existent main id, or a secondary whose content advances primary 1 carrying parent_main_id 2. good: parent_main_id 2 on a secondary whose content advances main objective 2.

created_at.description: UTC timestamp when objective was created (ISO 8601). Immutable.
created_at.$comment: Set once at creation. Never modify.

content.description: Specific verifiable outcome that contributes to ticket completion. Should be completable in a focused work session.
content.$comment: ONE verifiable step per secondary, completable+verifiable in one session. STOP: split it when multi-concern: a '+' or ' y '/' and ', a colon-list, a file/class inventory, two verbs, or a design choice on an em-dash. >180 chars is almost always more than one concern. REDIRECT: the how → completion_guide; the API surface → function_signatures; the scenarios → test_cases; a second deliverable → a SECOND secondary. bad: 'Crear UserRepository + UserDto + migración 011 + tests' (4 concerns). good: 'UserRepository.findByEmail returns the matching user or null' (one verifiable step; signature → function_signatures, scenarios → test_cases).

completion_guide.description: Step-by-step implementation guidance based on code analysis. References specific files, patterns, line numbers, and applicable rules + YAGNI principle applied to the design.
completion_guide.$comment: ONE concrete how-step per array item, each anchored to real code or a rule. STOP: split into two items when multi-concern: a '+'/' and ', a colon-list of actions, or two verbs in one string. >200 chars almost always = more than one step. REDIRECT: the WHY → the parent objective's context; the outcome being achieved → the objective's content; the acceptance proof → verification_demonstrations/test_cases. No generic advice; apply YAGNI per item. bad: 'Refactor the repo: add findByEmail using the pattern in user_repo.dart, then wire the DTO and add edge tests, because enterprise needs it' (steps + why + tests fused). good: 'Add findByEmail(String email) to user_repo.dart:45 following the existing findById query pattern; apply rule #7.'

function_signatures.description: Concrete function/method signatures this secondary creates or modifies. Real types — no 'any'/'dynamic'/'Object?'. Optional; omit for doc-only or greenfield-no-API secondaries.
function_signatures.$comment: DESIGN SPECIFICATION (design_principle #10). Forces confronting the real API surface at plan time, e.g. 'func (a *App) handlePaste(msg tea.PasteMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd)'. Generics are IN scope but MUST declare explicit type-parameter bounds (no unbounded any/dynamic/Object?/interface{} unless architecturally justified — put the justification in the secondary's content). A generic's correctness lives in its instantiations, so test_cases MUST include one edge_case row per concrete instantiation that matters. An unbounded generic with zero instantiation test_cases is the same blind spot as an unconsidered edge case.

test_cases.description: Behavioral scenarios this secondary must satisfy: happy paths + edge cases. DESIGN SPEC, not proof. Optional; populate for code-touching secondaries (design_principle #10, product_rule #10).
test_cases.$comment: test_cases SPECIFY behavior at design time and carry NO verdict. The primary's verification_demonstrations PROVE the suite passes (verdict=pass) by REFERENCE — enumerate once here, prove once there, no duplication (product_rule #10). A secondary touching shared state, async, or sibling handlers with ZERO edge_case:true rows is SUSPECT.

name.description: Identifier of the scenario (what is being tested), not of the implementation. e.g. 'paste during active probe', not 'test_handlePaste_1'.
name.$comment: Name the behavior/condition so the row is meaningful before any code exists.

input.description: Concrete trigger or precondition for the scenario. Optional for cases defined purely by state.
input.$comment: Be concrete: real values/events, e.g. 'PasteMsg arrives while state == probing'. Omit only when the scenario is fully described by name + expected.

expected.description: The behavioral contract: what MUST happen. For edge_case:true rows this is the forcing function — see $comment.
expected.$comment: When edge_case=true and this is EMPTY, the secondary is NOT ready and the logbook is BLOCKED. Filling it requires reading the sibling handlers/code to learn the invariant the new code must preserve. That empty->filled transition is exactly the work that catches relational runtime bugs (design_principle #10).

edge_case.description: THE forcing-function flag. true = boundary / concurrency / error-recovery / cross-handler-interaction case; false = happy path.
edge_case.$comment: Set true for any scenario at a boundary, under concurrency, on an error/recovery path, or that interacts with sibling handlers/shared state. An edge_case:true row with empty 'expected' blocks the logbook until resolved.

status.description: Current state: not_started (pending work), active (in progress), blocked (waiting on external input), achieved (completed), abandoned (cancelled).
status.$comment: Set only ONE secondary objective as 'active' at a time. Work sequentially. Set 'achieved' after verifying content statement is true in codebase.
